comment: Remotes KAT holds its own pictures and measurements of (remotes), and what KAT adds to an FCC filing's remote (fcc_extra). By hand. The pictures were sent in by the remotes' owners.

remotes.title: Opel two-button remote key
remotes.summary: An old two-button Opel remote key head: lock and unlock on one rubber pad with a red LED beside it. The board is dated 19 October 2000. KAT's [Opel Rolling](opel_rolling.md) protocol was worked out from recordings of this one remote.
facts: 433.89 MHz in the recordings; the board is printed `433MHz`
a bit is one period: 600 µs for a 0, 900 µs for a 1 (pause, then carrier, each half the period)
60 bits behind a sync of 300 µs carrier, 600 µs pause, 600 µs carrier
the frame three times; 57 periods of 600 µs before the first copy, 4 before the others
a 12-bit press counter under one of 16 masks, with a check nibble

chips.note: the immobiliser transponder in the same key head (marking read from a picture)

remotes.cars: Not known. The board's numbers match no part found so far. The two-button remote head of the Astra G and Zafira A of 1998 to 2005 is Bosch's RK 203 (Opel 93176615); a published write-up of a 2001 Astra's RK 203 describes another frame, so this remote is another unit or an earlier kind of that one. The transponder in the key head is the kind Opel keys of about 1998 to 2005 carry.

photos.credit: Sent in by the remote's owner.

remotes.title: Suzuki TS002 remote key (Calsonic Kansei)
remotes.summary: The two-button remote key Calsonic Kansei made for Suzuki; the case is marked "Calsonic Kansei Corp. TS002". KAT's [Suzuki TS002](suzuki_ts002.md) protocol was worked out from recordings of this one remote. Its code is not encrypted.
facts: 433.91 MHz in the recordings; a 433.92 MHz SAW resonator on the board
pulse width in cells of three units of 256.8 µs: a 0 is carrier 1, pause 2; a 1 is carrier 2, pause 1
72 bits and 72 one bits behind a sync of four units of carrier and four of pause
the frame four times; it goes on repeating while the button is held
the ID rotated by the press counter, next to the counter: not encrypted
remotes.cars: Not known. Parts sellers list TS002 remotes for the Suzuki Swift, SX4, Grand Vitara and Splash of about 2005 to 2014.

remotes.title: Renault one-button remote key (1999)
remotes.summary: An old one-button Renault remote key head; its board is dated 1999. KAT's [Renault 1-Button](renault_one_button.md) protocol was worked out from a recording of this one remote.
facts: Manchester, 473.5 µs per half bit (1056 bit/s)
70 bits behind a run of 0 bits: `11`, 24 fixed bits, 36 changing bits, an XOR check byte
the frame two to four times, 14 ms of pause and 8.7 ms of carrier between copies
36 bits that change with every press, with no structure found
`99 165`; an 8-pin chip marked `B 89AN`, `S1080`, `49004`; a SAW resonator
remotes.cars: Not known. One seller's listing of a one-button Renault remote quotes this chip marking together with the reference `S108627BN0`; another gives `S108627BN0` as the number on the board of Renault's one-button 433 MHz transmitter `7700438342` and lists it for the Mégane 1, Espace 3, Safrane and Laguna 1 (its title also names the Clio, Kangoo, Trafic and Master). Sellers' lists, not Renault's.

remotes.title: Delphi three-button remote (Peugeot / Citroën)
remotes.summary: A black oval remote with three buttons and "DELPHI" moulded into the case. It sends [PSA](psa.md) frames of the XOR type, and its recordings are what showed that PSA's two frame types number their buttons differently ([The Delphi remote](psa.md#the-delphi-remote)).
facts: two copies of one frame: about 173 preamble pulses before the first, 11 before the second
pads for four buttons; a 16-pin transmitter IC marked `5100 B2 0122`; a 13.560 MHz crystal; an 8-pin Microchip IC; a 3 V coin cell

chips.note: on the board, by its marking `5100 B2`

remotes.title: Valeo two-button key (Citroën / Peugeot)
remotes.summary: A two-button flip key for Citroën and Peugeot, made by Valeo: the case is moulded for both makes (`LION`, `CHEVRONS`). KAT's [PSA 2-Button](psa_two_button.md) protocol was worked out from recordings of this one key, a Citroën's. Its 76-bit frame is not the 80-bit frame of [PSA](psa.md).
facts: 433.9 MHz in the recordings: a 13.560 MHz crystal, times 32
Manchester, 207 µs per half bit (2415 bit/s)
76 bits behind half a bit of carrier, closed by 2.5 ms of carrier: `CE`, a button nibble, a 64-bit code
about 78 ms of carrier, 6.9 ms of pause, one frame
changes with every press; its bytes are XORs of the press counter, one more changing byte and values that stay. Not undone
a 20-pin NXP chip marked `22A1509`, `AZS5702`, `TnD3011`, `9221509`; a 13.560 MHz crystal; two switches

chips.note: the 20-pin chip on the board (marking read from a picture)

remotes.cars: Not known beyond the make: the recorded key is a Citroën's. The NXP logo on its chip puts it at 2006 or later.

remotes.title: Old VW flip key (VW-1)
remotes.summary: An old two-button Volkswagen flip key, the VW roundel on the back. KAT's [VW-1](vw_1.md) protocol was worked out from recordings of this one key. VW-1 is the oldest Volkswagen Group scheme — a 24-bit LFSR and a UID obfuscation, with no cipher — the "VW-1" of the study *Lock It and Still Lose It* (USENIX Security 2016). Not the newer 80-bit [VAG](vag.md) frame.
facts: pulse-width, 667 bit/s; one unit is about 500 µs
60 bits behind a 1500/1500 µs start: an obfuscated 32-bit UID, a 24-bit register, a button nibble
the frame two or three times, about 10 ms apart; presses about 90 ms apart
a 24-bit LFSR (feedback x²⁴ + x⁷ + x² + x + 1) clocked 23 times a press. There is no secret key, so a single capture gives the next valid code; KAT computes it
a 16-pin Motorola `ZC421689CDW` (`734 778-00`) on one side of board `734 613-02`; on the other an S+M `R707` SAW resonator, a 2.00 MHz ceramic resonator and the two switches
`HLO 1J0 959 753 A` on the unit that holds the board (`HLO` is Volkswagen's code for Hella; the label's edge reads `HELLA`), with European radio approvals dated 1998

chips.note: the controller on the board (marking read from a picture)

remotes.cars: A Volkswagen of roughly 1998–2005: the transmitter's `1J0` part number is of the Golf Mk4 / Bora / Jetta generation. The exact model year was not given with the recordings.

remotes.title: Renault Koleos four-button key (285970036R)
remotes.summary: The four-button key of the first Renault Koleos, Renault part `285970036R`, on a Continental board with an NXP PCF7941. KAT has no recording of it: this page comes from the key's own firmware, which KAT ran in its [MRK II emulator](mrk2.md). The key signs each press with HITAG2, in a frame KAT's decoders do not read yet; [Renault Koleos](renault_koleos.md) describes the frame and the code.
facts: NXP PCF7941 (ID46): radio remote and HITAG2 transponder in one chip
Manchester; the rate on air is not measured yet
a sync ending in `0x0001`, then 104 bits: a header byte, the 32-bit chip ID, the command, a repeat count and the counter's low 10 bits, a 32-bit keystream, an XOR byte
HITAG2 with a 48-bit key kept in EEPROM pages 4 and 5; IV = the 24-bit counter and the command
[Renault Koleos](renault_koleos.md), read from the firmware; no decoder yet

chips.note: the key controller, as parts sellers list it; its 4 KB firmware fits a PCF7941 (the PCF7952 runs 8 KB)

remotes.cars: Renault Koleos, first generation (built by Renault Samsung on a Nissan platform, sold from 2008), according to parts sellers.

photos.credit: Sent in by the remote's owner.

photos.credit: Sent in by the remote's owner.

chips.note: on the board, in the filing's internal photos and in a tester's key

M3N5WY72XX.note: A tester's four-button key of this FCC ID was recorded: 301 presses over six files, the sequence up by one per press ([Siemens 5WY72XX](siemens_5wy72xx.md#validation)).
